_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::contact#1, and a FALSIFICATION of its Signal. The rule holds — a mortar contact interface needs a Slave and a Master sharing an InterfaceID — but neither quoted log line exists in 4C ('no master partner found for interface X', 'MortarInterface: InterfaceID X has 0 master elements'), and CLAIMED_INTERFACE_TEXTS=0 pins that. Both real failures come from contact/src/4C_contact_utils.cpp, and the message depends on how the group is malformed rather than on which side is absent: marking both surfaces Slave gives 'Master side missing in contact condition group!', while listing only one surface gives 'Not enough contact conditions in discretization', which never names a side at all (ONESIDED_MESSAGE_NAMES_A_SIDE=no) and so reads like a missing-section problem instead of a missing-partner one. The paired control builds the interface and reaches a four-node active set. Distinct from the contact#0 fixture, which covers the two-Master and mismatched-ID cases. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) on a self-contained two-block penalty deck.
expect_in_output: Master side missing in contact condition group!
Not enough contact conditions in discretization

_mutation.note: remove the pathology from the two-Slave arm: give the second surface its Master role back. That arm then runs to completion and 'Master side missing' disappears, so the fixture must go red.
remove the pathology from the single-sided arm: list both surfaces. That arm then runs to completion and 'Not enough contact conditions in discretization' disappears, so the fixture must go red.
